simple.meaning: שָׁחַט (shâchaṭ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to slaughter (in sacrifice or massacre).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 82 times across Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Judges, and 9 more, beginning at Genesis 22:10. Its contexts include family line, altar, blood, death, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁחַט (H7819).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שָׁחַט (shâchaṭ) / H7819 is traced through Genesis 22:10, Genesis 37:31, Exodus 12:6, Exodus 12:21 as a generated source-based concept entry.
